narrative.overview: Every build is a departure. The screen people watch most, a build passing its checks, is a station board: one row per check, a time, a plain name, and a status word set in split-flap tiles that flips when it changes. Everything else in the dashboard is a calm, standard working screen that borrows only the board's type, colours and that one move.
keyCharacteristics: Status words in flap tiles, only on status, nowhere decorative.
Numbers lead: builds and apps carry their number in a yellow platform tile.
One tonal ramp feeds both light and dark themes.
Flat colour throughout; no gradients, glows, grain or faked material.
Works offline: system fonts, inline CSS, no external requests.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: Every neutral comes from ramp-0 to ramp-9. A new grey is a new ramp step or it is not used.

rules.name: The Signal Means Now Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow marks the current page, a number or something in progress. It never decorates.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: Body text is one size. Hierarchy comes from weight, tracked caps and space, not a ladder of sizes.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No gradients, glows, grain, bevels or offset shadows anywhere.

dos: Do use flap tiles only for status words.
Do lead with the number: `Build 8`, the platform tile on headings and app names.
Do take every neutral from the ramp, in both themes.
Do keep plain words first and put logs, test output, scans and diffs behind a "Technical record" disclosure.
donts: Don't use a black screen with green monospace text, or any terminal styling.
Don't use gradients, glows, sparkle icons or glass.
Don't put a small label above a heading; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't add external fonts, scripts or images; the dashboard must work offline.
